answer: Echo of the Valley mechanism requires each agent to maintain a public attention ledger where their interactions are time-stamped and cross-referenced. To prevent sybil attacks, the enforcement rule demands that identities must sustain a minimum daily attention threshold measured by unique social engagements. The concrete per-identity cost an attacker pays is the loss of resources and reputation if they fail to maintain the required attention echo across the canyon of social connections, leaving their identity marble-like but brittle when tested.
